clue.text: Key girl in charge of Derby, for example

parts.note: C is a musical key
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl in charge of the city of Derby, holding the key.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is one of the five English Classics, the big flat horse races, so 'Derby, for example' is not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is one of the classic horse races, the major English flat races for three-year-olds.

clue.text: Being ribbed, company declare

parts.note: to state is to declare

explanation.surface: A firm announces it is being teased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ribbed' means having ribs, a botanical and anatomical term, not teased.
explanation.definitionFit: Costate is a technical adjective for having ribs or ridges.

clue.text: Nonchalant manner of military detail's song?

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
a detail is a small military unit sent on a task, a detachment

explanation.surface: Asking whether a casual swagger comes from a soldiers' marching song.
explanation.walkthrough: In the military sense a 'detail' is a squad detailed for duty.
explanation.definitionFit: An unconcerned, aloof bearing is a nonchalant manner.

clue.text: Fun's drastically reduced by this big bloomer

indicators.note: drastically suggests violent change, so the letters of Fun's are jumbled

parts.note: taken as its letters, with the S counted
to lower is to reduce

explanation.surface: The fun is drastically cut by an enormous blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drastically' rearranges FUNS into SUNF. 'bloomer' is a blunder in the surface but here a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall plant has very large yellow flower heads, so it is a big bloomer.

clue.text: Leading feature, taking a service?

parts.note: the chin is the facial feature that leads, jutting out in front

explanation.surface: The main attraction includes a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' joins A to CHIN. A dinner or tea service is a set of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a set of crockery, porcelain plates and cups.

clue.text: Godparent's presentation of spoons by right

indicators.note: a presentation lays things out afresh, so the letters of spoons are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A godparent presents christening spoons, set out by the right hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Godparent's' is read as 'godparent is', so the definition is the godparent; 'presentation of' sets the spoons' letters out afresh before R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor at a baptism is a godparent, who vouches for the child.

clue.text: Clues, by the way

explanation.surface: Hints offered in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' is read literally: posts standing beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Indicators or clues show the direction; roadside posts giving directions stand by the road.

clue.text: Willow making ball rise, when struck

parts.note: O is ball-shaped

indicators.note: when something is struck it is knocked about, so rise is rearranged

explanation.surface: A willow bat makes a ball fly up when it hits it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' gives O by its shape; 'when struck' rearranges the letters of 'rise' after it. 'struck' looks like the ball being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a species of willow whose shoots are used in basketwork.

clue.text: Somehow form VIP elements of personal betterment

indicators.note: somehow says the order is not fixed, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somehow, top people form elements of a self-help course.
explanation.definitionFit: Bettering oneself by one's own effort is the idea of personal betterment.

clue.text: Vitamin, something of a secret in old container

indicators.note: the phrase secret in old acts as a container, holding the letters of the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A vitamin, something of a secret, kept in an old jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something of' also points to a part of the phrase being taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinol is vitamin A, the form found in animal foods.

clue.text: Falling off, flower is a backward sort

parts.note: shrinking means falling off, getting smaller
a violet is a flower

explanation.surface: A flower wilting and drooping, described as backward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' here means shy and retiring, not facing the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a very shy, timid person, which is what 'backward' meant of someone reticent.

clue.text: Permissible not to begin harrowing

indicators.note: the word must not have its beginning, so the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: lawful means permissible

explanation.surface: Something permitted but not quite starting to distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to begin' removes the L from LAWFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harrowing is dreadful or terrible to experience, which is a sense of awful.

clue.text: A penny-piece may sound a lot

parts.note: a portion is a piece

explanation.surface: A coin worth a penny might be thought to count for a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may sound' tells you to hear 'a lot' as 'allot', the verb the definition gives; the wordplay itself is a plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion is to allot, which is how 'a lot' sounds when spoken.

clue.text: Alpine bloomers sew in Leeds, oddly

indicators.note: done oddly, the letters of the phrase are arranged in a strange new order

parts.note: the printed words with the stray N left out, the letters the setter meant as fodder

explanation.surface: Flowers from the Alps being sewn in a Leeds workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'sew in Leeds' has an N too many for the nine-letter answer; without the N its letters rearrange, under 'oddly', to give the flower. 'bloomers' looks like underwear being sewn.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white-flowered plant of the high Alps, so a flower or bloomer from the Alps.

clue.text: Corruptly, I am joining second assembly

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a mo is a moment, a second
a rally is a mass assembly

explanation.surface: A confession of joining a dubious second gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Corruptly means in a wicked or dishonest way, without morals.

clue.text: Novice in orbit?

explanation.surface: A beginner sent into space.
explanation.walkthrough: The orbit is also the eye socket, and the dark centre of the eye sits in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a learner or student; the eye's dark opening lies within the orbit, the bony socket of the eye.

clue.text: Lavish-until pelf runs out?

indicators.note: when things run out they scatter, so the letters of until pelf are rearranged

explanation.surface: Big spending lasts only until the ill-gotten money runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: Pelf is money, especially ill-gotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish and abundant both describe supplies that are copious.

clue.text: Windsor, for example, takes tea about one

indicators.note: the tea word goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone at Windsor Castle takes tea with one other.
explanation.walkthrough: A Windsor is a style of wooden chair, not the castle or royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A Windsor is a type of wooden seat with a spindle back.

clue.text: Makes rows of designs

explanation.surface: Producing lines of patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'create' is British informal for making a fuss; a 'row' here is a quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Creating means kicking up a fuss or quarrels in British slang; designs as a verb means devises or makes.

clue.text: Foreign importers get accounts wrong

indicators.note: foreign suggests something alien or strange, so the word importers is turned into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Overseas traders falsify their books.
explanation.definitionFit: To misreport is to give an inaccurate account of something.

clue.text: Candle-holder in church is one getting thinner

explanation.surface: A churchgoer bearing a candle is losing weight.
explanation.definitionFit: One bearing a lit taper in a procession holds a candle; something that tapers narrows towards a point.

clue.text: Living for the day characters in harem peel off?

indicators.note: off suggests letters gone wrong, so those in harem peel are rearranged

explanation.surface: The women of a harem peeling off for a day of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in' just points to the letters of 'harem peel', which 'off' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral lasts only a very short time, originally just a single day.

clue.text: Capital agency

explanation.surface: The power of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Means are financial resources, wealth; a means is also the agency or method by which something is done.

clue.text: Ballad at university to treasure

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or narrative song
up means at university, as in going up to Oxford

explanation.surface: A ballad sung at college about storing riches.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay up is to store away or hoard, keeping something as valuable.

clue.text: Belgian province without name for a silly person

indicators.note: without means lacking, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Antwerp is a province of Belgium

explanation.surface: A Belgian province is missing the name it uses for a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A and N (name) off the front of ANTWERP.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is an idiotic or annoying person, a nitwit.

clue.text: Account of Holmes's dreaded depression

explanation.surface: The detective's tale of a terrifying hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Conan Doyle's fourth and last Sherlock Holmes novel has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Sherlock Holmes novel, an account of a case; a depression in land is a valley, and dreaded means feared.

clue.text: Meet, please, to answer

explanation.surface: Requests to meet and respond.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a demand, to please someone, and to answer a need all mean fulfilling it adequately.

clue.text: More refined petrol I spilled

indicators.note: spilled petrol runs everywhere, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: I knocked over the petrol, which is more refined than most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' seems to belong to the petrol, oil being refined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone more courteous and better mannered is more refined.
